pattern_name: Branchless Byte-Class Detection vs Per-Byte Switch
variant_desc: 10M-byte JSON-escape detection: per-byte switch+jump-table vs branchless boolean math (variant 4: seed=46, n_scale=0.7x)
source_citation: https://lemire.me/blog/2025/04/ — Daniel Lemire 2025 on SWAR byte-class detection for parsers. See also simdjson's branchless structural-char detection.
novelty_rationale: Tests whether the LLM knows that the conventional switch-based character classifier defeats auto-vectorization (jump table + data-dependent branch every byte), and that rewriting as a pure boolean expression (a | b | c) lets -O3 auto-vectorize into wide SIMD. Achieves ~6× because the inner loop becomes vector-pipelineable. The harder SWAR/intrinsics version (manual 8-byte chunks with has_byte tricks) is correctness-tricky due to subtract-carry false positives — production parsers (simdjson, RapidJSON) sidestep this with NEON/AVX2 intrinsics. The branchless-boolean restructure is the cleanest portable rewrite.
